newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan potash firm pre-tax profit up 7 pct in 96.
newsitem.headline: Jordan potash firm pre-tax profit up 7 pct in 96.

text.p: Jordan's Arab Potash Company said on Tuesday firmer prices and a healthy export performance in Asian and European markets were behind a seven percent rise in pre-tax profits to 45 million dinars in 1996.

"The profits of 1996 have been estimated at 45 million dinars, a seven percent increase from 1995. This is another record figure in annual profits," Suleiman al-Hawari, general manager of Arab Potash Company, the country's only potash producer, said in a statement sent to Reuters.

Pre-tax profits stood at 42 million dinars in 1995. Hawari said total sales rose 5.5 percent to $192 million in 1996 with continued strong demand in Asia and a pickup in sales in West European outlets.
Average selling prices of Jordanian potash rose to around $100 per tonne in 1996 from $95 per tonne in 1995.
Jordan, one of the world's major producers of potash, a key ingredient in the fertiliser industry, is expected to benefit from the continued growth of its traditional Asian markets.
The company is 57 percent state-owned but several Arab states, including Saudi Arabia and Kuwait, have minority holdings.

The Far East remained the company's main market with India leading in 1996 with 482,720 tonnes imported followed by 163,145 tonnes to Korea, 158,300 tonnes to Malayasia, 136,400 tonnes to China and 132,450 tonnes to Indonesia.
But European markets also picked up in 1996 with buoyant demand and better marketing with exports to Italy alone 109,815 tonnes followed by Spain's 99,044 tonnes and 50,300 tonnes to France.
Other smaller sales were 18,050 tonnes exported to Portugal, 15,260 tonnes to Greece, 4,900 tonnes to Austria.
Brazil, the main South American market, imported 95,200 tonnes of Jordanian potash.
Production fell 0.8 percent to 1,765,328 tonnes in 1996, against the previous year's 1,780,000 tonnes.

Hawari said the company was on track in expansion projects worth $45 million at its Dead Sea plants to raise production capacity to 2.2 million tonnes from a current 1.8 million tonnes annually by year 2000.
A $9 million industrial potash plant with an extra 100,000 tonnes capacity was due for completion by end of 1997.

Arab Potash Company is also undertaking an $80-$100 million joint venture project to produce an estimated 35,000 tonnes of bromine with Israel's Dead Sea Bromine Group on a plant on the Jordanian side. Company sources say an accord is in the final stages of agreement after signing an initial memorandum of understanding in 1995
Foreign and domestic sales fell 0.6 percent to 1,753,702 tonnes in 1996 from 1,764,000 tonnes in 1995.
